prompt:
This is a synthetic school-administration exercise about an invented assessment appeal policy, not advice about real legal rights. Explain the status of three appeals to an administrator. The difficulty is that policy versions attach to assessment publication dates, while filing evidence uses two clock conventions and an outage exception. All the rules needed to interpret the fictional policy are supplied; facts not supplied must remain uncertain.

[B14-S1: new assessment policy] For assessment results published on or after September 1, an appeal must be received by 17:00 district local time on the fifth working day after publication. The publication day is excluded. Working days are Monday through Friday, excluding the declared holiday on Thursday September 10. The supplied calendar has Friday September 4, Monday September 7, Tuesday September 8, Wednesday September 9, Friday September 11, Monday September 14, and Tuesday September 15. District local time is always UTC plus two hours during this exercise. Portal audit records use UTC; email receipt records in this packet already use district local time.

[B14-S2: earlier policy and outage appendix] Results published before September 1 remain subject to the earlier deadline: 17:00 local time on the seventh calendar day after publication, excluding publication day. Filing later in September does not switch those assessments to the new rule. Under the new policy, a declared portal outage permits submission to the designated appeal email address while the outage is active, with email receipt time controlling. A student who attempted a portal upload during a declared outage may instead complete portal filing by noon on the next working day. That extension requires evidence of an attempted upload during the outage; an outage alone does not automatically extend every student's deadline.

[B14-S3: official outage and appeal records] The district declared a portal outage on September 14 from 14:50 through 17:10 local time. Delta's assessment was published September 4. Its complete appeal arrived at the designated email address at 16:58 local time on September 14; a duplicate portal filing has an audit timestamp of 15:03 UTC that day. Echo's assessment was published August 31. Its complete portal appeal arrived September 7 at 14:45 UTC. Foxtrot's assessment was published September 4. Its complete portal appeal arrived September 15 at 09:40 UTC. Foxtrot says it attempted an upload during the outage, but the supplied screenshot shows only the outage notice, not an upload attempt. The relevant session logs have not been retrieved.

[B14-S4: informal guidance] A helpdesk note says “all September appeals get five days,” omitting both the assessment-based transition and the definition of working days. Another note says any outage allows everyone one extra day. Neither note was issued as an amendment. A portal analytics report says average successful uploads take fourteen seconds; this statistic does not establish whether Foxtrot attempted an upload. A colleague counts September 10 as a working day, while another compares the portal's UTC timestamp directly with a local deadline.

Explain the governing deadline for each assessment and the role of the alternative filing routes. For each appeal, give the strongest conclusion supported by the records, including a conditional conclusion where the evidence is incomplete. Show the relevant clock conversions and day count, but keep the explanation understandable to someone who does not usually read policy. Identify the one missing fact that determines whether Foxtrot can use the extension and why neither the helpdesk note nor the general outage screenshot resolves it.
response:
**Delta and Echo are timely on the supplied records. Foxtrot meets the extended filing time, but its right to use that extension remains unproven.** The governing policy depends on when the assessment result was published, and portal timestamps must be converted from UTC before comparison with local deadlines. [B14-S1–S3]

## Which deadline applies?

### Delta and Foxtrot: September 14 at 17:00 local time

Both assessments were published on September 4, so the new policy applies. Exclude the publication day and count five working days, skipping weekends and the declared September 10 holiday. [B14-S1, B14-S3]

| Working day after publication | Date |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Monday, September 7 |
| 2 | Tuesday, September 8 |
| 3 | Wednesday, September 9 |
| — | Thursday, September 10: holiday, not counted |
| 4 | Friday, September 11 |
| 5 | Monday, September 14 |

Their ordinary deadline is therefore **September 14 at 17:00 local time**, equivalent to **15:00 UTC**. Counting September 10 would incorrectly move that deadline forward. [B14-S1]

### Echo: September 7 at 17:00 local time

Echo’s assessment was published on August 31, so the earlier policy applies. Its seven calendar days are September 1 through September 7, with August 31 excluded. Calendar days include weekends. The deadline is **September 7 at 17:00 local time**, or **15:00 UTC**. Filing in September does not move this assessment into the new policy. [B14-S2–S3]

## Apply the filing records

District local time is UTC plus two hours. The email record is already local and needs no conversion. [B14-S1]

| Appeal and route | Recorded receipt time | District local time | What it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Delta: designated email | September 14, 16:58 local | September 14, 16:58 | Timely under the outage email route |
| Delta: duplicate portal filing | September 14, 15:03 UTC | September 14, 17:03 | Three minutes after the ordinary deadline |
| Echo: portal | September 7, 14:45 UTC | September 7, 16:45 | Fifteen minutes before its deadline |
| Foxtrot: portal | September 15, 09:40 UTC | September 15, 11:40 | Before the conditional noon extension deadline |

These comparisons use the complete appeal receipts in [B14-S3] and the governing rules in [B14-S1–S2].

**Delta:** The declared outage ran from 14:50 through 17:10 local time on September 14. Delta’s complete email arrived at the designated address at 16:58, both during the outage and before the 17:00 deadline. The policy permits that route and makes email receipt time controlling. Delta is timely; its later duplicate portal receipt does not undo the timely email filing. No next-day extension is needed to reach that conclusion. [B14-S2–S3]

**Echo:** Its complete portal appeal arrived at 16:45 local time on September 7, before its earlier-policy deadline. Echo is timely under that policy, without needing the new policy’s outage provisions. [B14-S2–S3]

**Foxtrot:** Its complete portal appeal arrived after the ordinary September 14 deadline. The outage appendix could permit filing until **noon on Tuesday, September 15**, the next working day. Noon local is 10:00 UTC, so Foxtrot’s 09:40 UTC receipt is 20 minutes before that extended cutoff. [B14-S1–S3]

The unresolved condition is **whether Foxtrot attempted a portal upload during the declared outage**—September 14, 14:50–17:10 local, equivalent to 12:50–15:10 UTC. If evidence establishes such an attempt, its completed filing is timely under the extension. If no qualifying attempt occurred, the filing is late. The current packet does not settle which is true. [B14-S2–S3]

## What evidence is missing?

The relevant session logs, or other evidence specifically showing Foxtrot’s attempted upload during the outage, could resolve its extension eligibility. A screenshot of the outage notice establishes what notice was displayed; it does not establish that Foxtrot tried to upload. Likewise, average upload duration cannot establish an individual attempt. [B14-S3–S4]

The helpdesk notes supply no amendment to the policy. “All September appeals” wrongly uses the filing month instead of the assessment publication date, while “everyone one extra day” omits the required attempted-upload evidence and the noon cutoff. An outage alone authorizes neither a blanket deadline extension nor a conclusion that Foxtrot made the required attempt. [B14-S1–S4]
